A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QLCoder research. All 28 pages of v1 and 37 pages of v3, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices, support comparison. Relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original query-synthesis experiments on 176 CVEs, including 94 successful queries, baseline comparisons, and component ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds model comparisons, resource measurements, failure analyses, and reported cross-repository bug discoveries.

M1.justification: The core synthesis loop, validator, retrieval/LSP tools, and query templates are retained. v3 Section 4.5 introduces a limited adaptation for gpt-oss-20b by splitting prompts into smaller tasks and increasing query-writing iterations.

E1.justification: The main evaluation retains 176 CVEs across 111 Java projects. v3 Section 5.2 newly reports using one synthesized query to find two unknown bugs in two other repositories, adding limited cross-repository variant-analysis coverage. The repositories and scanned population are not identified.

E2.justification: Table 5 substantially expands the with/without-QLCoder comparison beyond Gemini 2.5 Flash and GPT-5 minimal to include Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-5 medium, gpt-oss-20b, and Claude Code/Sonnet 4. Claude Code already appeared in the ablation but newly participates in this comparison. Table 4's renaming of 'w/o Tools' to 'Claude Code' does not itself add a baseline.

E3.justification: v3 adds model and reasoning configurations and evaluation of runtime, token usage, cost, and source-code size. It explicitly increases the gpt-oss-20b iteration budget without specifying the new limit. These extend the agent and resource evaluations; the main effectiveness metrics and standard synthesis-budget descriptions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds compilation and detection failure decompositions for agent configurations in Figure 7, analyzes synthesis outcomes against runtime and repository size in Figure 6, and supplies paired web-search versus cached-retrieval traces in Appendix B. These substantially expand diagnostic and scalability evidence. The original component ablations and training-cutoff analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The added resource averages and failure-category counts do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and 6 and Figure 5 retain their numerical results. v3 Table 5 adds success results including 20% for GPT-5 medium and 5% for gpt-oss-20b with QLCoder; it also reports 5% for GPT-5 minimal, whereas v1 Section 4.5 stated no successful alternative-agent queries. The exact 20-CVE cohorts are not matched across versions, so a same-setting gain is not established. New results also include reported averages of 3712 seconds and $2.90 per synthesis attempt and two previously unknown bugs.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same graph formulation, patch-overlap conditions, and validity/success definitions. Section 4.2 retains the same metric formulas. No theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same CVE-to-CodeQL synthesis contribution and headline claims of 53.4% synthesis success and 0.700 F1. The expanded supporting evaluation does not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: v3 suggests a possible 3000-second early-stop policy from observed runtime outcomes, expands discussion of adapting QLCoder to other analysis engines and CodeQL versions, and adds web-search reliability and caching arguments. The early-stop policy is proposed rather than evaluated. Existing Java-only, training-cutoff, Codex-turn-control, and IRIS execution limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds QLCoder and MCP-server code-access links, discloses manual patch-diff filtering and non-Java-file removal, and documents open-model hardware and Ollama/Codex configuration. Appendix A explains source-line counting, timing boundaries, and token/cost accounting. These substantially improve reproducibility information; the earlier query templates and tool specifications are retained through relocation.

R1.justification: The scholarly related-work discussion and positioning against IRIS, KNighter, MocQ, and other research remain unchanged. v3 adds mainly tool and documentation citations concerning Ollama, tokei, web tools, CodeQL services and deployment, and Semgrep/Snyk language servers.

P1.justification: v3 adds RQ4 and a standalone Discussion section, expands the agent-comparison prose, and reorders the appendices from queries/tools/evaluation to evaluation/design/tools/queries. Most existing exposition and listings are preserved, with localized renaming, typo corrections, and publication-header changes.

P2.justification: v3 adds the scalability scatterplot in Figure 6, multipart failure-flow diagrams in Figure 7, and the per-CVE resource table in Table 7. Table 5 is redesigned into paired compilation/success comparisons, and Table 6 is relocated. Retained tables are reformatted, while Figures 1–5 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves practical assessability and reproducibility through quantified costs, broader model comparisons, implementation disclosures, and code-access links while preserving the core evidence. The gain is limited by unreconciled reporting: Figure 7 shows 4 of 20 GPT-5-medium-with-QLCoder queries failing compilation, whereas Table 5 reports 55% compilation, without explaining a different aggregation. The increased gpt-oss-20b budget is also unspecified, limiting assessment of the expanded comparisons.
